hook.line: Altamira wants the park, and everyone on the block has an opinion about it. Judging something (it's a shame, it's important, it's normal) is the most natural way to say what you think, and Spanish gives it a verb form of its own.
hook.es: Es una pena que cierren el parque.
hook.en: It's a shame they're closing the park.

examples.en: It's important that you read it. (to a friend)

examples.es: Es una pena que cierren el parque.
examples.en: It's a shame they're closing the park.

examples.es: Es normal que Simón grite por la mañana.
examples.en: It's normal for Simón to yell in the morning.

examples.es: Es bueno que ustedes estén aquí.
examples.en: It's good that you all are here.

examples.es: No es justo que ellos cobren tanto.
examples.en: It's not fair that they charge so much.
It's necessary that you pay today. (to a friend)

examples.es: Es importante que Tomás abra temprano.
examples.en: It's important that Tomás opens early.

rule:
Each of these lines gives a judgement: good, important, normal, fair, a shame. The judgement is the first part (*Es importante*, *Es una pena*, *Es normal*), then *que*, then what happens.

The verb after *que* takes the wish form, the same one you met with *quiero que* and *me alegra que*: *leas*, *cierren*, *grite*, *estén*.

English says *is*, *are*, *reads*. Spanish switches to the wish form because you are judging the thing, not reporting it.

The same pattern works for *Es mejor que esperemos* (it's better that we wait), *Es bueno que*, *Es necesario que* and *No es justo que*.

If you mean people in general, skip *que* and use the plain verb: *Es normal tener miedo.* *Es mejor llamar antes.*
smallPrint: Teachers call this the subjunctive after expressions of judgement (*subjuntivo con expresiones de valoración*). Facts such as *es verdad que* work differently, and you'll see why in the next drill.

options: It's important that you read it. (to a friend)
It's important that I read it.
It's important that she reads it.
It's normal that they're afraid.
It's normal to be afraid.
It's normal that I'm afraid.
It's necessary that I pay today.
It's necessary that we pay today.
It's necessary that you pay today. (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: Es bueno que ustedes estén aquí.
options: It's good that you all are here.
It's good that they are here.
It's good that we are here.

readAndPick.es: Es importante que Tomás abra temprano.
options: Tomás says it's important to open early.
It's important that Tomás opens early.
It's important for me to open early.

readAndPick.es: Es una pena que no puedas venir.
options: It's a shame I can't come.
It's a shame she can't come.
It's a shame you can't come. (to a friend)

It's important that everyone votes.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *pagas* or *pagues* and type the whole sentence, to a friend: *Es necesario que tú ___ hoy.*
yourTurn.answer: Es necesario que tú pagues hoy.
yourTurn.why: A judgement like *es necesario* is followed by the wish form: *pagues*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *puede* or *pueda* and type the whole sentence: *Es una pena que Vale no ___ venir.*
yourTurn.answer: Es una pena que Vale no pueda venir.
yourTurn.why: *Es una pena que* is a judgement, so *pueda*, not *puede*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It's important that Tomás opens early.
yourTurn.answer: Es importante que Tomás abra temprano.
yourTurn.why: *Es importante que* takes the wish form of *abrir*, which is *abra*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It's normal to be afraid.
yourTurn.why: It's about people in general, so no *que*: just the plain verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It's a shame they're closing the park.
yourTurn.answer: Es una pena que cierren el parque.
yourTurn.why: *Una pena* is a judgement, and *cierran* becomes *cierren*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Es justo que ellos cobren tanto.*
yourTurn.answer: No es justo que ellos cobren tanto.
yourTurn.why: Only *no* is added. The verb stays in the wish form.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it to you all instead: *Es importante que lo leas.*
yourTurn.answer: Es importante que ustedes lo lean.

pitfalls.why: Almost. After a judgement, use the wish form: *leas*, not *lees*.

pitfalls.wrong: Es normal que Simón grita por la mañana.
pitfalls.right: Es normal que Simón grite por la mañana.
pitfalls.why: You are judging it, not just reporting it, so *grita* becomes *grite*.

pitfalls.wrong: Es una pena cierren el parque.
pitfalls.right: Es una pena que cierren el parque.
pitfalls.why: Spanish needs *que* here, even though English can drop *that*.
When it is about people in general, use the plain verb and no *que*.

personal: Say two true judgements about your own neighbourhood, one with *Es una pena que* and one with *Es importante que* (*Es una pena que el parque...*, *Es importante que los vecinos...*).
